lessons.title: How doctors diagnose PsA

pages.body: There is no single test for PsA. Doctors look at your joints, skin, nails and X-rays together.
Your doctor may also ask if anyone in your family has psoriasis. Blood tests can help rule out other kinds of arthritis.

key_takeaways: There is no single test for PsA.
Doctors combine exams, family history and tests.

claims.text: There is no single test for PsA.
claims.source_quote: There is no single test that confirms psoriatic arthritis.

claims.text: Doctors look at joints, skin, nails and X-rays together.
claims.source_quote: Diagnosis combines the exam of joints, skin and nails with X-ray findings.

claims.text: Doctors may ask about psoriasis in the family.
claims.source_quote: Family history of psoriasis is part of the assessment.

claims.text: Blood tests can help rule out other kinds of arthritis.
claims.source_quote: Blood tests are used to help exclude other types of arthritis.

lessons.title: Nail and finger clues

pages.body: Some changes to the nails can be a clue to PsA. Small pits in the nail or a nail that lifts from the nail bed are examples.
Dactylitis is a swollen finger or toe that looks like a sausage. It is common in PsA.

key_takeaways: Nail changes can be a clue to PsA.
Dactylitis is a sausage-like swollen finger or toe.

claims.text: Pits in the nail or a nail that lifts from the nail bed can be clues to PsA.
claims.source_quote: Nail pitting and onycholysis (lifting of the nail) are common in psoriatic arthritis.

claims.text: Dactylitis is a swollen finger or toe that looks like a sausage.
claims.source_quote: Dactylitis is a diffusely swollen digit, often called a sausage digit.
Dactylitis is a common feature of psoriatic arthritis.

pages.body: X-rays can show changes in the joints. Your doctor may repeat them over time to see if the joints are changing.

claims.text: X-rays can show changes in the joints.
claims.source_quote: Plain X-rays can show joint changes in psoriatic arthritis.

claims.text: An ultrasound is needed to confirm PsA.
claims.source_quote: Plain X-rays can show joint changes in psoriatic arthritis.
